sources.title: Opening our newest data center in Los Lunas, New Mexico
IM3 Open Source Data Center Atlas, release 2026.02.09

research_updates.title: Boundary and operating chronology verified
research_updates.notes: IM3 record 00626785488 is one 654,433-square-foot mapped footprint within a multi-building Los Lunas campus and supplies no building name or public-record crosswalk. State and Village records date the first campus groundbreaking to October 2016, the first online building to 2017, a campus grand opening to February 7, 2019, and six online buildings to 2022. They do not identify which chronology belongs to the selected footprint. The later 2021 two-building expansion, the three-building expansion load described in 2023, the 2025 AI expansion, tenant equipment, off-site renewable projects and other Meta facilities remain outside the selected-building boundary.

source.title: IM3 Open Source Data Center Atlas, release 2026.02.09
source.notes: The selected inventory object is IM3 building record 00626785488, a 654,433-square-foot mapped footprint at 34.830246608460115, -106.78382909936067. IM3 separately maps four other buildings and a campus polygon at the Los Lunas site; the record does not provide a building name, construction cost, opening date, parcel, permit or utility-account crosswalk.

research_updates.title: Original incentive authorization is not realized value
research_updates.notes: The June 23, 2016 bond package and Ordinance 407 were reviewed for original-project terms. Authorization for as many as six $5 billion industrial-revenue-bond series is a financing ceiling, not issued principal, capital expenditure, tax abatement, cash grant, property-tax saving or public cost. Later 2021 and 2025 bond packages concern expansions and are excluded. No selected-building bond draw, lease payment or realized incentive value was located.

source.title: Village Council agenda package, June 23, 2016, Ordinance 407
source.notes: The original Greater Kudu industrial-revenue-bond package authorizes up to six series of as much as $5 billion each for construction and equipping of the data-center campus. Those maximum principal amounts are legal authorization ceilings, not issued debt, expenditure, capital investment, subsidy or realized tax benefit.

research_updates.title: Campus parcel is fully exempt in the 2023 assessor revision
research_updates.notes: The exact address resolves to Village-owned UPC 1006040261023 / account R302913, a 738.15-acre campus parcel with business name FACEBOOK. The 2023 County fields report $19,930,050 actual value, $6,643,350 total assessed value, an equal other exemption and zero net assessed value. Those stocks are retained at unallocated campus scope; they are not a cash estimate of tax savings. Village FY2017-FY2023 GASB 77 schedules separately mark the Greater Kudu agreement under construction and PILOT receipts N/A for the school district, State and County. The report's unrelated $450,000 Village-wide PILOT total is excluded, and no selected-building or personal-property account, bill, payment, taxing-jurisdiction receipt, lease revenue, service cost or net fiscal result was found.

source.title: Valencia County parcel record for 4250 Messenger Loop NW
source.notes: The County's live ArcGIS parcel service resolves the exact campus address to UPC 1006040261023 and account R302913, a 738.15-acre parcel owned by the Village of Los Lunas with business name FACEBOOK. Revision-year 2023 fields report $19,930,050 actual value, $6,643,350 total assessed value, an equal $6,643,350 other exemption, and zero net assessed value. The parcel contains the full campus and does not crosswalk the selected IM3 footprint or identify a personal-property account, tax bill, payment, taxing-jurisdiction distribution or cash value of taxes foregone. A separate owner-name result for Greater Kudu is a 2022-recorded 474.35-acre tract and is outside the original selected-building boundary.

research_updates.title: Public-cost search supports fund flows with scope limits
research_updates.notes: Village budgets from FY2017 through FY2025, Resolution 16-26, the 2021 PPA amendment and dedicated infrastructure accounts were searched for State LEDA, Local LEDA GRT, Facebook, Greater Kudu and Meta flows. The original formula dedicated 75% of specified Village gross-receipts-tax distributions attributable to construction. Actual State LEDA receipts total $10 million across FY2017-FY2018; FY2021 actual outlays are $2,043,636 in the State project fund and $1,130,805 in the local fund. The FY2024 NM 6 traffic account separately reports $529,277 of revenue and $23,200 of capital purchases, and Village records identify Meta as payer for the completed off-site system. Receipts and expenditures are separate flows and are not summed or netted. The 2021 amendment says Greater Kudu declined some reimbursements and the Village would contract directly for revised infrastructure, but gives no dollar reconciliation. None of these funds is an IM3-building allocation or a complete marginal public-cost account.

source.title: Village of Los Lunas FY2022 Final Budget
source.notes: The budget reports FY2021 actual expenditures for both the State LEDA Facebook Project Fund and the Local LEDA GRT Fund. The local fund receives transfers tied to project-attributable gross-receipts-tax distributions but finances water-system and rail-park projects with wider service areas.

research_updates.title: Permit, planning, construction and fire searches lack an IM3 crosswalk
research_updates.notes: The Village planning and zoning agenda archive, development-plan and permit page, fire-prevention and public-works access points, and state Construction Industries Division portal were searched for 2016-2026. The exact campus address returned 20 state records: 11 electrical, five mechanical, three general-construction and one modular record, with 13 closed and seven issued statuses. Their 2021-2026 labels use VCN, VLL6, later halls, administrative or temporary work; one detail page records a passed 2024 security final inspection, but no record supplies an IM3 crosswalk, permit fee or certificate of occupancy. No selected-building permit valuation, fee, inspection, construction start or contractor-payment value can be established, and post-2020 work is not used as original-building evidence. Complete applications, approved plans, fee receipts, inspection histories and certificates remain records-request targets for CID and the Village.

source.title: New Mexico public permit search
source.publisher: New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department, Construction Industries Division
source.notes: An exact-address query returned 20 records dated 2021-2026: 11 electrical, five mechanical, three general-construction and one modular record. Project labels include VCN 1A-1B, VCN 1C-1D, VCN 2, VCN ADMIN, VLL6, later data halls, a prefabrication tent, an art project and a power box; statuses comprise 13 closed and seven issued records. Detail pages expose application-entered scope, contractor and selected inspection fields, but an IM3 project-name query returned no records and no building crosswalk, permit fee, certificate of occupancy or selected-footprint valuation was found.

research_updates.title: Water agreement supplies capacity, not use
research_updates.notes: The original and restated agreement recitals, the August 2021 water-connection agreement, Village project-status and budget records, state water-right access and public water-planning materials were reviewed. The original 303-acre property received up to 500 acre-feet per year of consumptive water rights, converted to 0.446371233 million gallons per day for the direct record. A later Tank 7 connection was budgeted at $995,000 and Greater Kudu agreed to pay all design, construction and observation costs, but neither item is a realized payment and both remain unallocated campus infrastructure. The agreement's 4.5-million-gallon worst-case delivery guarantee and 1.5-million-gallon wastewater ceiling are capacities, not use; the reported 153,000-gallon 2020 campus average could not be tied to a public meter record. Village meter histories, bills, reimbursement ledgers, connection invoices and OSE diversion records remain request targets.

source.title: Village Council agenda package, February 13, 2025, amended and restated Greater Kudu water and wastewater agreement
source.notes: The restated agreement recites the October 4, 2016 original agreement for the 303-acre original property and its allocation of up to 500 acre-feet per year of consumptive water rights. It also states contractual peak service and wastewater limits, which are capacities rather than metered use. The added 2019 property and 2025 AI expansion are excluded.

research_updates.title: Electric utility and regulatory searches isolate no building account
research_updates.notes: PNM and NMPRC materials for the original special-service contract and cases 16-00191-UT, 18-00269-UT, 21-00031-UT, 23-00251-UT and 25-00048-UT were reviewed. The 2018 notice confirms Greater Kudu's contribution-to-production mechanism, Meta's payment guaranty and customer recovery of specified renewable PPA costs, but supplies no realized dollar amount. Public versions do not disclose an IM3-building utility identity, meter, demand, consumption, bill, payment, customer contribution in aid of construction or original-campus interconnection outlay. PNM meter histories, billing determinants, invoices, receipts and interconnection work orders remain request targets; off-site or expansion-linked renewable-project spending, landowner payments and jobs are excluded.

source.title: PNM regulatory filings for Greater Kudu special-service contracts
source.publisher: Public Service Company of New Mexico
source.notes: Public filings for NMPRC Cases 16-00191-UT, 18-00269-UT, 21-00031-UT, 23-00251-UT and 25-00048-UT were searched. They document special-service and renewable-energy arrangements, later expansion loads and customer-paid renewable resources, but no public selected-building meter, demand, consumption, bill, rate payment or original-campus utility-infrastructure outlay.

research_updates.title: Environmental permit is site-wide and non-operational
research_updates.notes: New Mexico Environment Department air applications, permit notices, facility and emissions registries, compliance histories and feasibility materials were searched for Greater Kudu, Meta, 4250 Messenger Loop, agency interest 37303 and permit 7026 from 2016-2026. The 2024 application carries forward 118 permitted stationary generators plus two temporary units for the full source and distinguishes VLL from later VCN groups, but the public copy omits the referenced plot-plan appendix and supplies no IM3 crosswalk. Compliance tables list NOx, CO and opacity test dates from 2019-2023 without results; the state EPA-reporting layer returns no exact-name or exact-address record. The permitted count is retained as a site-wide stock, while potential emissions, ratings and tests do not prove runtime, diesel use, actual emissions, electric load, water use or environmental damages. NMED inspection reports, test results, annual emissions, excess-emission reports, tank and stormwater files remain request targets.

source.title: Greater Kudu LLC Air Quality Permit 7026-M6 original application
source.notes: The operating-facility application covers the full 4250 Messenger Loop source and carries forward 118 stationary emergency generators while replacing two units, plus two temporary portable units. Its unit schedule distinguishes original VLL1-VLL6 groups from later VCN groups and reports construction or installation years, but the plot-plan appendix is not included in the public copy and no group is crosswalked to IM3 record 00626785488. Compliance-history tables list required NOx, CO and opacity test dates from 2019-2023 but no test results or actual annual emissions. Potential emissions and permit limits are not runtime, fuel use, actual emissions or utility consumption.

research_updates.title: Operator, SEC and workforce sources retain payroll gaps
research_updates.notes: Meta's 2019 opening release, current Los Lunas materials, 2021 expansion release, 2025 Form 10-K, New Mexico economic-development and Workforce Solutions reports, BLS OEWS access and current job postings were searched for headcount, occupation, wage, payroll, residence and hiring evidence. The opening release supports more than 150 campus jobs, while a 2018 state review repeats forecasts of 800-1,000 daily construction workers through 2023 and about 300 permanent jobs at full six-building operation; forecasts are not actuals. No source identifies filled selected-building headcount, direct versus contractor status, FTEs, wages, benefits, worker residence, occupations or hiring dates. Current 400-plus job and $2.5-billion campus figures include or anticipate later expansion and are excluded; statewide or Albuquerque-area occupation wages are not substituted for Meta payroll.

source.title: Meta Platforms, Inc. 2025 Form 10-K
source.notes: The filing reports company-wide capital expenditure, headcount and global data-center properties. It does not disclose Los Lunas building-level expenditure, depreciation, operating expense, payroll, employment, suppliers, property tax, utilities or grants.

research_updates.title: Supplier and procurement searches produce identities, not payments
research_updates.notes: State economic-development reports, Village budgets, operator releases, CID permits and searches for Fortis, APIC Solutions, Southland Industries, Cache Valley Electric, B&D Industries and other named contractors were reviewed. The records identify contractors, equipment providers and construction activity but disclose no contract value, invoice, payment date, local purchasing share, supplier payroll or selected-building allocation. The separate $37 million PNM solar contract and renewable-project construction statistics concern off-site generation, not Los Lunas data-center supplier spending, and are excluded.

source.title: New Mexico Economic Development Department FY2018 Annual Report
source.notes: The state chronology reports the first Los Lunas data-center groundbreaking in October 2016, a doubling to two buildings in July 2017, and a six-building, 330-acre campus announcement in September 2017. It does not map those buildings to IM3 record 00626785488.

research_updates.title: Community and recipient records support non-additive grants
research_updates.notes: Village newsletters and agendas, Meta grant materials, the 2023 PNM filing appendix and recipient reports from Explora and named schools and nonprofits were reviewed for 2017-2026. Direct observations retain Meta's greater-than-$3.1-million cumulative Valencia County funding through June 2023, the $225,000 Wi-Fi grant and the $212,000 arithmetic sum of 17 May 2023 awards. These company-county figures overlap and must not be summed or assigned to the selected building. Meta's November 2025 program update reports more than 210 Los Lunas-area grants and sponsorships since 2019 but no local dollar total; a May 2026 Village quorum notice confirms another ceremony without amounts. Recipient sources generally confirmed relationships but did not disclose additional exact amounts, payment dates, restricted balances or building attribution.

source.title: Village News, May 2023
source.notes: The Village lists 17 Meta Community Action Grant recipients and an amount for each. The arithmetic sum is $212,000; it overlaps Meta's cumulative direct-funding disclosures and is not a selected-building amount.

research_updates.title: County outcomes and residual modeling remain unsupported
research_updates.notes: The direct-evidence audit ends with no residual model because no public record identifies when IM3 footprint 00626785488 opened or separates its construction and operations from the five other original campus buildings. The first building was online in 2017, the campus opened publicly in 2019, and six buildings were online by 2022, creating staggered treatment alongside other Valencia County developments and later Meta expansion. BLS QCEW county and industry files, BEA county accounts and Census workforce access were checked as potential comparison series, but they cannot identify the selected building, direct versus contractor employment, worker residence or a defensible treatment date; simultaneous county development and disclosure suppression add further limits. Without building-level capital, employment, payroll, supplier, utility and fiscal anchors, a county difference, multiplier, avoided-cost or residual estimate would manufacture precision. No synthesis fragment is created.

source.title: Village of Los Lunas FY2023 Final Budget
source.notes: The Village reports that Meta's first building went online in 2017 and six buildings were online by 2022, with two more planned. The later two-building expansion and its stated area and investment are outside the selected-building boundary.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. project_description: Meta Los Lunas is a Meta-operated data-center campus at 4250 Messenger Loop NW in the Village of Los Lunas, Valencia County, New Mexico; the selected project is the individual IM3-mapped 654,433-square-foot building footprint, not the full campus. State and Village records show the campus broke ground in October 2016, its first building was online in 2017, and Meta held a campus grand opening on February 7, 2019 while an original six-building program was still being built. The boundary excludes the separately announced 2021 two-building expansion, the 2025 AI expansion, off-site renewable projects, tenant equipment, and other Meta facilities.
